 Rennais head into Nice carrying genuine momentum after a 3-0 dismantling of Strasbourg, a result that offered the first real evidence this squad can impose itself in Ligue 1. The problem is that two points from three league matches still leaves them 15th in the table, and a trip to the Allianz Riviera demands they back up that performance immediately. Nice, sitting 11th with four points, are not exactly flying either, but they have the home advantage and a striker who has been one of the more reliable finishers in the division.
 Elye Wahi leads Nice’s attack with three goals and nine shots on target — numbers that reflect a forward who is not just getting chances but converting them. For Rennais, Esteban Lepaul has been extraordinary: seven goals and 14 shots on target make him one of the most dangerous forwards in the league right now, and his ability to drag a team up the table almost single-handedly gives Rennais a genuine weapon regardless of context.
 Both sides need points. Both have players capable of deciding a match on their own. That combination tends to produce football worth watching.

 Game Preview
 Nice sit 11th in Ligue 1 with four points and a goal differential of -1, a position that reflects a team still searching for consistency rather than one that has found its level. Rennais are 15th with two points and a -2 goal differential, meaning neither side can afford to treat this as a low-stakes fixture. A win for Rennais would close the gap significantly and signal that the Strasbourg result was a turning point rather than an outlier. For Nice, dropping points at home to a side below them would deepen concerns about their own form.
 What to Watch For
 Esteban Lepaul is the player every opposition defender in Ligue 1 has circled on the team sheet. Seven goals and 14 shots on target through the early weeks of the season put him in a category of his own among Rennais attackers, and the supply lines around him are credible — Adrien Thomasson has created 13 chances and contributed two assists, while Sebastian Szymanski brings three goals and four chances created of his own. Rennais are not a one-man team, even if Lepaul is the focal point.
 For Nice, the question is whether Wahi can find the same efficiency he has shown in patches. Three goals and nine shots on target suggest a forward who is getting into the right positions, and Jonathan Clauss has been one of the more active creators in the squad with 10 chances created. Mohamed Amoura adds another dimension — a goal, an assist, nine chances created — giving Nice multiple ways to threaten.
 The midfield battle could be decisive. Valentin Rongier has nine chances created and a goal for Rennais, while Gauthier Hein’s nine chances created give Nice a comparable engine in the middle. Whichever midfield controls territory is likely to dictate the tempo.
